newsitem.title: DUBAI: Dubai MTBE plant hit by poor returns - trade.
newsitem.headline: Dubai MTBE plant hit by poor returns - trade.

text.p: Dubai Natural Gas Co Ltd (DUGAS) has temporarily suspended operations at its 500,000 tonnes a year capacity MTBE plant because of weak MTBE export markets and strong feedstock prices, Gulf oil traders said on Thursday.
"The plant has been forced to shut down. It's just not profitable enough for them to operate at the moment...The plant will be back when profits return," one regional trader said.

A DUGAS official who declined to be identified said that the plant at the Jebel Ali free trade zone in the UAE emirate of Dubai was shut for normal maintenance work. He would not give further details.
Other DUGAS officials also declined comment.
The MTBE plant came onstream in 1995 with the aim of capitalising on an expected growth in demand for the gasoline-additive methyl tertiary-butyl ether (MTBE).
MTBE is an octane enhancer that allows the elimination of lead from petrol.
Industry sources said that the $250 million-plus plant last underwent maintenance in the fourth quarter of last year.
Supplies of liquefied petroleum gas (LPG) from DUGAS's gas plant were not affected by events at the MTBE plant, lifters and traders in the Gulf said.
